description: Finding 3. Replace the hostname-string-only SSRF guard and the redirect-following global fetch in the link-preview feature with a DNS-aware, redirect-aware, address-pinned fetch built on node http/https (no new dependencies). Public signature/return shape of isSafePreviewUrl, extractMeta, linkPreviewCache, LINK_PREVIEW_TTL and the JSON shape of GET /api/link-preview stay the same. Independent of FEAT-001/002. Full design: plan section F3.
steps: Rewrite lib/link-preview.js internals (keep header comment style, keep exporting linkPreviewCache, LINK_PREVIEW_TTL, isSafePreviewUrl, extractMeta; add exports isBlockedAddress, createSafeLookup, createPreviewFetcher, fetchPreview). Implement exactly per plan F3: (1) isBlockedAddress via net.BlockList with the IPv4 and IPv6 ranges listed there, fail-closed for non-IP input, zone id stripped, IPv4-mapped ::ffff:0:0/96 blocked wholesale; (2) sync isSafePreviewUrl(parsed): http/https only, normalized host (brackets/trailing dot stripped, lowercase), reject empty, localhost, *.localhost, single-label hosts, and blocked IP literals (new URL already canonicalizes 0x7f.0.0.1 / 2130706433 / octal forms); (3) createSafeLookup(dnsLookup = dns.lookup, isBlocked) validating ALL resolved addresses (reject if any blocked or none), supporting both options.all true and false callback styles, calling dns.lookup through the module object so tests can stub it; (4) createPreviewFetcher({ lookup, isBlockedAddress }) -> fetchPreview(rawUrl, { timeoutMs = 6000, maxChars = 300000, maxRedirects = 3 }): manual redirect loop (301/302/303/307/308 + Location), re-run isSafePreviewUrl on each hop, mod.request(url, { agent: false, lookup, headers }) with the existing User-Agent/Accept headers plus Accept-Encoding gzip, deflate, br, decode with zlib, also re-check res.socket.remoteAddress, one overall 6 s timer cleared when final headers arrive, read at most 300000 chars via TextDecoder only for text/html (non-HTML body is not read), resolve { finalUrl, contentType, html }, do not reject on non-2xx.

routes/chat.js: change the L15 require to also import fetchPreview; replace the AbortController/timer/fetch/reader block (L426-455) with `const page = await fetchPreview(parsed.href);` and use page.contentType, page.html and page.finalUrl in place of response.headers content-type, the streamed html and `response.url || parsed.href`. Leave cache keys, the non-HTML data object (image: contentType.startsWith('image/') ? parsed.href : null), extractMeta usage, 500-entry cap, the demo-mode early return, and the catch block (cache an empty preview and answer 200) untouched. Add a short comment: hosts that resolve or redirect to private addresses yield the same graceful empty preview; literal private IPs still get the 400 from isSafePreviewUrl.

Write the temporary script tmp-ssrf-check.js in the worktree root implementing the case list in plan F3 Verification: all private literals/IPv6/mapped/odd-IP forms and file:/ftp: rejected; dns.lookup stubs returning 127.0.0.1, a mixed [public, private] list, and ::ffff:10.0.0.5 rejected; redirect from a local test server (hop 1 allowed via a stateful injected isBlockedAddress that exempts 127.0.0.1 for the first hop only) to http://169.254.169.254/ and to a hostname stubbed to 127.0.0.1 rejected; >3 redirects rejected; allowed public example (https://example.com with dns.lookup stubbed to 93.184.216.34, validator only, no real network) accepted; full fetch+HTML parse (and a gzip body) against a local test server returns { finalUrl, contentType, html } and extractMeta works. Exit non-zero on any failed assertion; run it with node and require exit code 0 / all assertions printed as passed.

Route-level check with the fake-DB harness (non-demo, NODE_ENV=development): GET /api/link-preview?url=http://127.0.0.1/ and http://169.254.169.254/ -> 400 with `Ten adres nie jest obsługiwany`; unauthenticated -> 401; missing url -> 400 `Brak adresu URL`. Demo mode (OFFLINE_MODE=true): ?url=https://example.com returns the empty-preview JSON with no outbound request.
node --check lib/link-preview.js routes/chat.js. Delete tmp-ssrf-check.js and any other tmp-*.js.

Commit: `git add lib/link-preview.js routes/chat.js` by name only, message e.g. `fix(security): Harden link preview against SSRF`, body explaining DNS validation of all addresses, per-hop redirect checks and address pinning, no sim trailer, do not push. Set status completed and record findings (the case table results and the consequence that private-resolving hosts return a 200 empty preview).
acceptance_criteria: Every private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT/unspecified/multicast address, IPv6 equivalent and IPv4-mapped IPv6 form is rejected, both as a literal and when returned by DNS (even if only ONE of several resolved addresses is private)
Octal/hex/decimal IP tricks are rejected; file: and ftp: schemes are rejected

A redirect from an allowed host to a private target (IP literal or hostname resolving privately) is rejected, redirects are capped at 3, and the connection uses only the addresses that were validated (custom lookup, agent:false)
Legitimate public URLs still work: the stubbed public host is accepted, the local-server fetch returns finalUrl/contentType/html and extractMeta parses it

Timeouts (6 s to headers) and the 300000-char body cap are preserved; isSafePreviewUrl keeps its sync boolean signature and the route's JSON shapes and error messages are unchanged; package.json untouched
verification: node tmp-ssrf-check.js exits 0 with every case asserted (then the file is deleted)
Fake-DB route-level link-preview checks give 400/401/400 as specified; demo-mode request returns the empty preview
findings: Committed as ceb255d on fix/harden-server-1 (lib/link-preview.js, routes/chat.js; 196+/32-; not pushed; CRLF preserved, bareLF=0). node --check OK on both. tmp-ssrf-check.js: 63 assertions, exit 0, then deleted (plus tmp-fakedb.js, tmp-route-check.js). CASE TABLE: REJECT literals via isSafePreviewUrl (28): 127.0.0.1, localhost, foo.localhost, [::1], 0x7f.0.0.1, 2130706433, 017700000001, 127.1, 169.254.169.254, 10.0.0.5, 172.16.0.1, 172.31.255.255, 192.168.1.1, 100.64.0.1, 0.0.0.0, 0.1.2.3, [::ffff:127.0.0.1], [::ffff:7f00:1], [::ffff:8.8.8.8], [fc00::1], [fd12::1], [fe80::1], [::], 224.0.0.1, single-label 'intranet', file:, ftp:, 127.0.0.1. (trailing dot). ACCEPT: https://example.com, http://93.184.216.34, public IPv6 literal, sub.example.co.uk. isBlockedAddress fails closed for non-IP, strips %zone, public v4 not blocked. DNS validator (createSafeLookup) rejects with code ESSRF_BLOCKED for 127.0.0.1, mixed [93.184.216.34, 10.0.0.5], ::ffff:10.0.0.5 and empty list in all call styles (all:true, all:false, no options); accepts public in both styles; default dns.lookup stub via module object works; default fetchPreview rejects hosts stubbed to 127.0.0.1 / mixed / mapped, and literal 127.0.0.1 and file:. Redirects (local server, stateful isBlockedAddress exempting loopback only for the local.test hop): 302 to http://169.254.169.254/ rejected, 302 to evil2.test (stubbed 127.0.0.1) rejected with ESSRF_BLOCKED, 302 to file: rejected, chain >3 rejected after exactly 4 requests, same-host 301 followed (finalUrl = final hop). Fetch path: html+extractMeta OK; gzip, br and deflate bodies decode; image/png not read (html ''); 404 does not reject; 900000-char body capped (~327k chars, chunk granularity, same as before) and maxChars option honoured; 500 ms header timeout rejects; strict fetcher without exemption rejects the loopback-resolving local server. ROUTE LEVEL (fake DB, DB_PASSWORD=x NODE_ENV=development, login via POST /api/login): unauthenticated 401; ?url=http://127.0.0.1/ 400 and ?url=http://169.254.169.254/ 400 and ?url=http://[::ffff:7f00:1]/ 400, all with 'Ten adres nie jest obslugiwany'; no url 400 'Brak adresu URL'; a real GET of https://example.com returned 200 with title 'Example Domain' (real network, https + content-encoding path works end to end). Demo (OFFLINE_MODE=true): ?url=https://example.com returns the empty preview {url,title:null,description:null,image:null,siteName:'example.com'} (early return, no outbound request); literal private IPs still 400. NOTES/DEVIATIONS: (1) net.BlockList matches IPv4 addresses against IPv4-mapped IPv6 rules (::ffff:0:0/96 blocked every IPv4 address in the first run), so there are two lists (blockedV4, blockedV6) and the v6 list uses ::/96 (unspecified, loopback and deprecated IPv4-compatible) instead of separate ::/128 and ::1/128 entries; mapped ::ffff:0:0/96 is still blocked wholesale for IPv6 inputs. (2) isSafePreviewUrl gained an optional 2nd argument (isBlocked, default isBlockedAddress) used by the fetcher's test seam; one-arg calls and the boolean return are unchanged. (3) CONSEQUENCE: hostnames that resolve to a private address, or redirect into one, now yield the graceful empty preview (HTTP 200, cached as {url,title:null,image:null,siteName}) from the existing catch block, not a 400; literal private IPs still get 400. A comment in routes/chat.js documents this. (4) The overall timer is cleared on final headers (as before); body reading has no separate timer, same as the old fetch code. package.json, public/, .agents/ untouched in the commit.
